entry.title: We are heading to the Bernstein Conference with 1 workshop, 4 Talks, and 4 posters!

link.title: We are heading to the Bernstein Conference with 1 workshop, 4 Talks, and 4 posters!

entry.content:
Join us at the Bernstein Conference for a workshop, four talks, and four posters exploring adaptive behavior, decision-making, and neural dynamics.

Workshop:

  • From lab to wild: how internal states enable adaptive behavior (Sep 28–29, Claire and Arman)

Talks:

  • Emergent animal-like foraging and functional circuits in neural networks trained with homeostatic reinforcement learning (main meeting, Sep 30, Shervin)
  • Criticality, neuromodulatory state, and the computational machinery of perceptual decision-making (workshops, Sep 28, Shervin)
  • Neural, computational, and behavioral mechanisms of internal decision processes (workshops, Sep 28, Shervin)
  • Optimal foraging under naturalistic temporal dynamics (workshops, Sep 29, Roxana)

Posters:

  • Identifying internal states by temporal embedding of dynamics in biological and artificial neural networks (poster session II, Sep 29, Arman)
  • Foraging minds: computational and neural foundations of internal decision processes (poster session II, Sep 29, Claire)
  • Fast dynamical similarity analysis (poster session II, Sep 29, Arman)
  • Behaviorally-relevant decomposition of neural dynamics during naturalistic decisions (poster session IV, Sep 30, Max)

entry.title: New paper at Trends in Cognitive Sciences

link.title: New paper at Trends in Cognitive Sciences

entry.content:
Our new paper on “Perceptual multistability a multifaceted window into brain dysfunctions” is now out in Trends in Cognitive Sciences.

Highlights:

  • Perceptual multistability is a well-established phenomenon that has been studied for at least a quarter of a millennium and has inspired a wealth of findings in neuroscience and psychology.
  • It holds potential for advancing our understanding of psychiatric disorders and neurodiversity, as differences in perceptual inference and dynamics are observed across a broad range of clinical/non-clinical populations. Furthermore, it can synergize with recent advancements in computational psychiatry, in particular, transdiagnostic approaches.
  • Novel computational frameworks can integrate classical Bayesian and recent reinforcement learning approaches and provide a framework to explain these differences and bridge cognitive and neural mechanisms.
  • Given the translational potential of multistability, it can also be a promising experimental tool to link malfunctioning computations to underlying neurobiology in animal models of psychiatric disorders.

You can check out the details here.

entry.title: CMC lab presentations at Cosyne 2026
entry.content:
We presented 3 exciting posters at Cosyne 2026!!!

  1. “Unsupervised identification of behaviorally-relevant neural states with non-linear temporal embeddings”. Arman Behrad, Maximilian Schwabe, Christian Beste, Shervin Safavi.

  2. “Revealing task-relevant dynamics via decomposition of intrinsic and input-driven dynamics”. Maximilian Schwabe, Arman Behrad, Roxana Zeraati, Shervin Safavi.

  3. “Koopman-based transient dynamics reconstruction”. Anima Kujur, Zahra Monfared, Shervin Safavi.
